title: Marvell launches connectivity chips for AI infrastructure
source_used: Marvell newsroom press release of 13 Oct 2026 (investing.com page returned HTTP 403); GuruFocus read for context
key_facts: Marvell announced on 13 Oct 2026 two connectivity chips for AI scale-up infrastructure: the Alaska E 3.2T retimer and the second-generation Alaska A 1.6T AEC DSP.
Alaska E is a protocol-aware Ethernet, UALink and ESUN retimer with 16 lanes of 224G PAM4, giving 3.2 Tbps of bandwidth.

Alaska A (second generation) moves to the 3nm node for 1.6T active electrical cables and enables copper reaches exceeding six metres, doubling the first generation; Marvell cites 12.8 W power and eight watts saved against 5nm designs.
Both devices are now sampling to customers; the announcement gives no booked volumes (GuruFocus).
Vladimir Kozlov, founder and CEO of LightCounting, is quoted saying the AI scale-up networking market will exceed USD 50 billion by 2030.
Marvell shares traded about 2.3% lower on the day (GuruFocus), which notes customer sampling is an early milestone that does not show revenue.
quote_evidence: Marvell Technology, Inc. (NASDAQ: MRVL), a leader in data infrastructure semiconductor solutions, today announced two additions to its advanced connectivity portfolio designed to meet the rapidly increasing bandwidth, reach and power-efficiency requirements of AI scale-up infrastructure.
Availability: Alaska E 3.2T protocol-aware retimer and second-generation Alaska A 1.6T are now sampling to customers.

The Alaska A 1.6T AEC DSP addresses this need by enabling AI fabric connectivity at 1.6T throughput over longer copper reaches exceeding six meters, doubling the reach of the first-generation product.
why_it_matters_hint: Faster, longer-reach links inside AI racks are needed as systems pack in more accelerators.
notes: Source is Marvell's own press release (investing.com carried it and was blocked). Performance figures are Marvell's claims. Sampling is an early stage.
